audit.why: EVEN diff, 5.5/10 difficulty is reasonable — Tahm's engage (Abyssal Dive, W) is the swing tool and Lulu's Q outranges his Q, matching the packet's mixed level chart.
Level 3 (Whimsy online) and Level 6 (Wild Growth vs Devour) and first item (HP stacking blunts poke) are the real spikes per both kits.

audit.whatIsWrong: content whys[4] names 'Abyssal Voyage' as Tahm Kench's level-6 spike ability — no such ability exists in his kit. His R is Devour (cd 0, needs 3 stacks or the R itself grants access); Abyssal Dive is his W, not the level-6 power.
audit.why: A fabricated ability name shipped to the page; this is exactly the class of error called out in the calibration examples (Brand's R, Cassiopeia's Q).
audit.corrected: Replaced with Devour (R), the real level-6 threat: an all-in/save tool with no cooldown that either removes an ally from danger or threatens a pick, which is what actually trades against Wild Growth.

edits.before: Q the doubled angle, E-mark the carry, auto — Pix volleys the chip while your buttons wait for the real question.
edits.after: Land E on your ADC before Tahm hits three Tongue Lash stacks — Pix's extra damage keeps you ahead without you walking into Q range.

edits.before: Polymorphing poke out of irritation and meeting the engage with a shrug — the W is the matchup.
edits.after: Tahm's grey-health passive (Thick Skin, E) heals back chip damage out of combat — don't score the trade off his HP bar alone.

edits.before: - Tahm Kench Abyssal Dive: matchup-defining — His re-engage and his escape — all-in only while it is down. The duo’s tempo bends around it. - Keep W Whimsy banked for their best play. - The ultimate is a fight decision, not a habit.
edits.after: - Tongue Lash (Q): 7s at rank 1 down to 5s at max — three stacks stun your ADC, so track his mark count. - Abyssal Dive (W): 21s down to 17s — his re-engage and escape; all-in only while it's down. - Devour (R) has no cooldown but needs range or 3 stacks — a fight decision, not a habit.

edits.before: Q the doubled angle, E-mark the carry, auto — Pix volleys the chip while your buttons wait for the real question.
edits.after: Glitterlance's 925 range beats Tongue Lash's 900 — poke first, E-mark your ADC's target, and let Pix volley the chip while he closes the gap.

edits.before: Polymorphing poke out of irritation and meeting the engage with a shrug — the W is the matchup.
edits.after: Trading toe-to-toe once he's landed two Tongue Lash stacks — the third Q stuns your ADC straight into Devour range.

edits.before: Ahead, squirrel the comeback: poly Tahm Kench's every play, grow the carry, and zone with Pix chip.
edits.after: Ahead, deny his stacks: Whimsy him the moment he's tagged your ADC twice with Tongue Lash, and push objectives while Abyssal Dive is down.

edits.before: Tahm Kench wins by landing Abyssal Dive, denying your pattern, and starting one clean chain and letting it pay the whole lane.
edits.after: Tahm Kench wins by landing Abyssal Dive into a 3-stack Tongue Lash stun, then Devouring your ADC before Wild Growth can save them.

edits.before: Good trade: Q the doubled angle, E-mark the carry, auto — Pix volleys the chip while your buttons wait for the real question. Bad trade: Polymorphing poke out of irritation and meeting the engage with a shrug — the W is the matchup.
edits.after: Good trade: poke with Glitterlance's longer range and E-mark the target before he closes in. Bad trade: standing still after two Tongue Lash stacks — the third stuns into a Devour.

edits.before: Level 3 poly re-prices 2v2s; level 6 deletes burst math; first item compounds the kit.
edits.after: Level 3 poly cancels a landed stun chain; level 6 Wild Growth answers a Devour dive; his HP stacking blunts your poke at first item.

edits.before: At 6 it is skill: Abyssal Voyage repositioning trades against your Wild Growth.
edits.after: At 6 it is skill: Devour threatens a pick or saves an ally, trading against your Wild Growth.
